Seven identical dice (each with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 points on their faces) are glued together to form the solid shown. Faces that are glued together each have the same number of points. How many points can be seen on the surface of the solid?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows seven cubes arranged as a 3D cross: one central cube has cubes attached in the six coordinate directions—left, right, front, back, top, and bottom. The back cube is only partly visible behind the arrangement, while the other attached cubes are more clearly visible. Reasoning: Each die has faces numbered 1 through 6, so the total number of pips on one die is 1+2+3+4+5+6=21. For 7 dice, the total pips on all faces before gluing is 7×21=147. The central die has all six of its faces glued to the six surrounding dice, so all of its face values 1,2,3,4,5,6 are hidden. Their sum is 21. For each glued face on the central die, the matching glued face on the outer die has the same number of points, so the six hidden faces on the outer dice also sum to 21. Thus the total hidden pips are 21+21=42. Visible pips = total pips − hidden pips = 147−42=105. Final answer: 105

Then use the text fact that each die has faces numbered 1 through 6, and whenever two faces are glued, the two glued faces have the same number. Compute the total number of pips on all dice as 7 × (1+2+3+4+5+6) = 147. The central die has all six of its faces glued, so its hidden glued-face values are 1,2,3,4,5,6. Each outer die is glued to the central die on a face with the same value, so the total hidden pips are 2 × (1+2+3+4+5+6) = 42. Subtract hidden pips from total pips: 147 − 42 = 105 visible pips.
